entities.name: Roald Amundsen
entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Roald Engelbregt Gravning Amundsen (1872–1928) was a Norwegian explorer who led the first expedition to reach the South Pole on December 14, 1911, beating Robert Falcon Scott's British team by 34 days. He was also the first to traverse the Northwest Passage by ship (1903–1906) and is generally considered the most successful polar explorer in history.

Amundsen's South Pole success rested on meticulous preparation, Inuit survival techniques (dog sleds, fur clothing), and a relentless focus on efficiency. While Scott's team perished on their return journey, all five members of Amundsen's party returned safely.

In 1926, Amundsen led the first verified expedition over the North Pole by airship (the Norge), making him the first person to reach both poles. He disappeared in 1928 while flying a rescue mission for the airship Italia in the Arctic, his body never recovered.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: Amundsen's achievement marked a significant milestone in polar exploration, demonstrating the feasibility of traversing the globe by airship and solidifying Norway's position as a major maritime power. His success paved the way for future expeditions and inspired generations of explorers.
